name: Grey
summary: Progressive loss of pigment from the hair with age, caused by extra copies of a 4.6 kb sequence in intron 6 of STX17. A foal is born its base colour and whitens over the years, often to nearly white; the genes for its base colour are unchanged underneath. Dominant: one G2 or G3 allele is enough. G3 carries three copies of the sequence, greys fast and raises the risk of melanoma. G2 carries two, greys slowly, and in the one study that separated them showed a melanoma incidence like that of non-grey horses. UC Davis calls the wild-type allele G1.

alleles.name: Fast grey, three copies of the sequence
Slow grey, two copies of the sequence

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: The coat keeps its colour for life.

phenotypes.name: Slow grey (G2 without G3)
phenotypes.description: Greys slowly. Born its base colour, the horse gains white hairs gradually and is typically still a moderate grey in middle age.

phenotypes.name: Fast grey (one G3)
phenotypes.description: Greys quickly. Born its base colour, noticeably grey or dappled as a young adult, and usually white or nearly white in later life. Where the second allele is G2 the pace is less well characterised.

phenotypes.name: Fastest grey (G3/G3)
phenotypes.description: Two G3 alleles: the fastest greying and the highest melanoma incidence.

conditions.name: Melanoma risk (raised)
conditions.description: One G3 allele. A raised incidence of melanoma, mostly tumours in the skin under the tail, around the anus and genitals, and on the head. With G2 as the second allele the size of the risk is less well characterised.

conditions.name: Melanoma risk (highest)
conditions.description: Two G3 alleles: the highest melanoma incidence of any genotype at this locus.

frequencies.population: Andalusian (allele frequencies G2 0.05 and G3 0.36 in the 2024 copy-number study's sample; genotype shares worked out from them)
